author: Akien (observation), CC (capture + the one instrumented reading)
text: Akien, at the close of this session: when this claude was started up he first looked and it was hovering around 450-550MB, going up and down; a couple of hours later it is 600-700MB. Sliding very slowly upwards — roughly 200MB over a couple of hours. He explicitly notes he did NOT record the time or the amount at start, which is precisely the gap the ticket the-memory-curve-is-recorded-not-eyeballed exists to close: this is a real observation at n=3-ish with no timestamps under it, so it cannot yet distinguish a leak from a working set that grows with a long conversation and then plateaus. Worth capturing anyway — under Law 10 a recorded observation IS a measurement, and a coarse one is a thing to sharpen rather than nothing.

the_one_reading_that_does_have_a_timesta.method: VmRSS from /proc/350050/status, start time from ps -o lstart=
the_one_reading_that_does_have_a_timesta.note: One point, not a curve. It sits inside Akien's eyeballed 600-700MB band and is consistent with his ~200MB/2h slope, but a single RSS reading cannot establish a slope, a plateau, or a leak — that is the ticket's job.

why_this_matters_beyond_tidiness: n=3 on this laptop the claude binary has reached ~12-14GB and globally OOM-killed the box, taking the whole Konsole scope with it (memory claude-oom-kills-the-box). superclaude now caps it in its own cgroup, so the blast radius is bounded — but a slow upward slide is the early part of the curve nobody has ever actually plotted, and the cap turns a crash into a kill without telling anyone what the shape was.
not_a_decision: This is capture, not a finding. Nothing here says there IS a leak.
